academic_translation: Subhūti, the name of this Dharma discourse is the perfection of wisdom;
translation: Subhuti, the name of this lesson on the teaching is perfect wisdom, the perfection of wisdom;

academic_translation: you should hold it thus.
translation: You should remember it like this.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, because the very perfection of wisdom spoken by the Tathāgata is itself not a perfection.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, because the perfect wisdom spoken by the Thus-Gone One is itself not a perfection.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called the perfection of wisdom.
translation: That is why it is called perfect wisdom, the perfection of wisdom.

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever spoken by the Tathāgata?
translation: Do you think there is any thing at all spoken by the Thus-Gone One?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata."
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, there is no thing at all that the Thus-Gone One has taught."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think that the particles of earth that exist in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system are many?"
translation: "Do you think there are many specks of earth in this world realm, a universe of a billion worlds?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, those particles of earth are many.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, there are many of those specks of earth.

academic_translation: Sugata, they are many.
translation: Well-Gone One, they are many.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a particle of earth has been taught by the Tathāgata as not a particle,
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because the Thus-Gone One has taught that whatever is a speck of earth is not a speck,

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called a "particle of earth."
translation: That is why it is called a 'speck of earth.'

academic_translation: Because whatever those world systems are, the Tathāgata has taught them as non-systems.
translation: Because whatever those world realms are, the Thus-Gone One taught that they are not realms.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called a "world system."
translation: That is why it is called a 'world realm.'

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: Do you think the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha should be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?
translation: "Do you think the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha should be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great person?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: "Blessed One, that is not so."
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: "Why is that? Because whatever thirty-two marks of a great man were spoken of by the Tathāgata, they were spoken of by the Tathāgata as no marks.
translation: "Why is that? Because when the Thus-Gone One spoke of the thirty-two marks of a great person, the Thus-Gone One spoke of them as no marks.

academic_translation: Therefore they are called the thirty-two marks of a great man."
translation: That is why they are called the thirty-two marks of a great person."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, someone who takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teaches it properly to others would, on that basis, generate far greater merit than that, incalculable and immeasurable."
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, imagine a man or woman gives away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River. Now imagine someone takes just a four-line verse from this lesson on the teaching and teaches it well to others. That person would create much more stored-up goodness from it. It would be too great to count or measure."

academic_translation: Then venerable Subhūti shed tears by the force of the Dharma.
translation: Then the honored Subhuti cried because of the power of the teaching.

academic_translation: Having wiped away his tears, he said this to the Blessed One:
translation: He wiped away his tears and said this to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, it is a marvel how extensively this Dharma discourse has been spoken by the Tathāgata. Sugata, it is a marvel.
translation: Blessed One, it is a marvel how fully the Thus-Gone One has spoken this lesson on the teaching. Well-Gone One, it is a marvel.

academic_translation: Blessed One, ever since pristine wisdom arose in me, I have never before heard this Dharma discourse.
translation: Blessed One, ever since deep knowing awoke in me, I have never before heard this lesson on the teaching.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, those sentient beings who will generate a true perception regarding this sūtra being explained will be endowed with supreme marvel.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, those living beings who form a true idea about this sacred text being explained will be filled with the greatest wonder.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a true perception is itself a non-perception.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a true idea is itself an absence of ideas.

academic_translation: Therefore, the Tathāgata speaks of 'true perception'.
translation: That is why the Thus-Gone One speaks of a 'true idea'.

academic_translation: Blessed One, that I contemplate and have faith in this Dharma discourse being explained is not a marvel to me.
translation: Blessed One, it is no marvel to me that I think about and trust this lesson on the teaching.

academic_translation: Blessed One, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and fully master this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme marvel.
translation: Blessed One, in the future, during the last five hundred years, some living beings will take up, write, hold, keep, read, and fully master this lesson on the teaching. They will be truly amazing.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Blessed One, they will not engage in the perception of a self,
translation: Also, Blessed One, they will not have the idea of a self.

academic_translation: and will not engage in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person.
translation: They will not have the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, or the idea of a person.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because, Blessed One, whatever is the perception of a self, the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, and the perception of a person, that itself is devoid of all perceptions.
translation: Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the idea of a self, the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, and the idea of a person are all free from ideas.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are devoid of all perceptions.
translation: Why is that? Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are free from all ideas.

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: After he said this, the Blessed One spoke to honored Subhuti:

academic_translation: Subhūti, so it is. So it is.
translation: "Subhuti, it is so. It is exactly so.

academic_translation: Those sentient beings who, when this sūtra is being explained, are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely frightened, will be endowed with supreme marvel.
translation: Any living beings who are not scared, frightened, or terrified at all when this sacred text is explained will be truly amazing.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, the Thus-Gone One taught this highest perfection.

academic_translation: because whatever supreme perfections were taught by the Tathāgata, those were also taught by immeasurable, countless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
translation: This is because whatever highest perfection the Thus-Gone One taught was also taught by countless, endless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.
translation: That is why it is called the highest perfection.
